Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

SPECIFICATION FOR 
PINS AND WIRES, SKELETAL, TRACTION 

PART II GUIDE WIRES 



1- Scope — Dimensional and other requirements for skeletal guide wires used in association with 
other devices, such as cannuiated hip nails in orthopaedic surgery, 

2. Shape and Dimensions — As shown in Fig. 1. 

j— THREE FACED END, 30° INCLUDED ANGLE p-DlA 2-5 ^l-AT 



-^ 



^ 



-225- 



Aii dimensions in millimetres. 
FIG. 1 GUIDE WIRES, SKELETAL 

2.1 A deviation of ±2'5 percent shall be allowed on all dimensions. 

2.2 Ends — The point shall be of the trocar pattern not exceeding the diameter of the wire and with 
three faces set at an included angle of 30° with the shaft. Diamond points with an included angle of 
45° may be provided, if required. The end opposite the point shall be flat. 

2.3 Diameter — Guide wires shall be designed to fit thecannulae of hip nails with a minimum clearance 
of 0*25 mm. The diameter of the guide wires shall be 2*5 mm (see IS : 1137-1959 Specification 
for thicknesses of sheet and diameters of wires). 

2.4 Length— Guide wires shall be supplied in lengths of 225 mm, or as specified by the purchaser. 

2.5 Graduation — Guide wires shall be graduated at intervals of 15 mm. The graduations shall be 
markedly etching. 

3. Material — Shall be austenitic stainless steel, wrought cobalt-chromium alloy or titanium alloy in

ments of metai surgicai impiants '" and shaii meet the requirements of the corrosion resistance test as 
given in 6.1.1 of IS : 5347-1969. 

3.1.1 Condition — The wires shall be in the cold drawn conditon but may have received stress reliev- 
ing treatments a temperature not exceeding 450° C. 

3.1.2 Tensile strength — The minimum tensile strength shall be 1 550 N/mra 2 . 

3.2 Wrought Cobalt-Chromium Alloy — Shall be in accordance with A-3.1 of IS : 5347-1969.

3.2.2 Tensile strength — The tensile strength of guide wires shall not be less than 1 280 N/mm 2 .

3.3.1 Condition — The guide wires shall be in the cold drawn condition and centreless ground. 

3.3.2 Tensile strength — The tensile strength shall be between 1 150 N/mm 2 and 1 400 N/mm a . 

4. Hardness 

4.1 The guide wires shall have a hardness of 200 to 300 HV.

IS: 8261 (Part II)- 1976 

5. Workmanship and Finish 

5.1 The guide wires shall be free from seems, laps, draw marks, cracks, pits, etc. The guide wires 
shall not be brittle. 

5.2 Unless otherwise stated, the wires shall be well polished. 

6. Marking 

6.1 The packet containing guide wires shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the following: 

a) Manufacturer's name, initials or recognized trade-mark; 

b) Name of the material; and 

c) Size. 

6.2 ISI Certification Marking— Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 

7. Packing 

7.1 As agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier.
